extracted.intended_audience: public housing authorities (PHAs), HUD-assisted property owners and managers, landlords, housing legal advocates, and HUD staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final HUD regulatory text and responses to comments establishing requirements for 30-day notice procedures for nonpayment-of-rent terminations across specified HUD programs (public housing, PBRA, certain Section 8 programs), including required notice content, timing, lease addenda, responsibilities, and scope/coverage limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day notice timing — termination effective no earlier than 30 days after receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: When termination is based on nonpayment of rent (and in other specified cases), the termination notice shall be effective no earlier than 30 days after receipt by the tenant of the termination notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text appears at §247.4(c) and repeated in program-specific provisions (e.g., §880.607(c)(6), §884.216(d), etc.). For other 'good cause' terminations, notices are effective at the end of a term in accordance with the rental agreement but in no case earlier than 30 days after receipt. For material noncompliance or failures under state landlord-tenant law, timing is in accord with the rental agreement and state law. HUD explains this balances tenant opportunity to cure and program/owner interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on issuing termination notice before day after rent is due
rubrics_metrics.description: The landlord/owner must not provide tenants with a termination notice prior to the day after the rent is due according to the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated explicitly in §247.4(c) and repeated in program sections (e.g., §880.607(c)(7), §884.216(e)). Intended to prevent premature notices issued before the rent is officially delinquent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filing eviction if tenant pays within 30-day notification period
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner/landlord must not proceed with filing a formal judicial eviction if the tenant pays the alleged amount of rent owed within the 30-day notification period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly required in §247.4(c) and repeated elsewhere (e.g., §880.607(c)(7), §884.216(e)). This is linked to the 30-day effectiveness period to allow tenants time to cure nonpayment and for owners to refrain from filing while cure is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity requirement — notice must state dollar amount and date of computation
rubrics_metrics.description: In any case initiated because of failure to pay rent, a notice stating the dollar amount of the balance due on the rent account and the date of such computation shall satisfy the requirement of specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out in §247.4(e) (introductory text) and replicated in program sections. This is the baseline specificity; additional required content (see other metrics) further explain cure instructions and arrearage breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must include instructions to cure including itemized monthly arrears and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: All termination notices in cases of nonpayment of rent must include instructions on how the tenant can cure the nonpayment, including an itemized amount separated by month of alleged rent owed by the tenant, any other arrearages allowed by HUD and included in the lease separated by month, and the date by which the tenant must pay the amount of rent owed before an eviction for nonpayment of rent can be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required in §247.4(e)(1) and mirrored in other parts (e.g., §880.607(c)(6)(i), §884.216(d)(1)). The itemization by month and inclusion of other HUD-allowed arrearages are required to improve clarity for tenants and courts and to help tenants know exactly what must be paid to avoid eviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must include information on recertification and hardship exemptions (24 CFR 5.630(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination notices must include information on how the tenant can recertify their income and, for tenants in projects assisted pursuant to a housing assistance payments contract for project-based assistance under section 8, information on how the tenant can apply for a hardship exemption pursuant to 24 CFR 5.630(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified at §247.4(e)(2) and repeated in program-specific provisions (e.g., §880.607(c)(6)(ii), §884.216(d)(2)). HUD underscores that explaining recertification/hardship processes helps tenants seek relief (interim recertification, hardship exemptions) that may prevent eviction. HUD also notes PBV owners generally do not recertify income, and PHAs are responsible for ensuring PBV families understand how to request recertifications/hardship exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must include Secretary-required information during Presidential national emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a Presidential declaration of a national emergency, termination notices must include such information to tenants as required by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out at §247.4(e)(3) and in corresponding program sections. HUD indicates the final rule provides flexibility to require emergency-specific information depending on circumstances of a given national emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease/addendum must state tenants receive at least 30 days' notice before formal judicial eviction
rubrics_metrics.description: The lease must contain a provision or addendum that tenants will receive notification at least 30 days before a formal judicial eviction is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New or revised lease-language requirements are added across multiple parts (e.g., §880.606(b), §884.215, §886.127(c), §886.327(c), §891.425(d), and analogous changes to part 966). HUD will supply the information that providers must give to tenants; incorporating this provision into leases ensures contractual notice rights and consistent practice across covered program types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only lease signatories to be named in termination and court documents
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs and owners must ensure that only signatories of the lease are named in the 30-day notification, any lease termination notices, and subsequent court documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD emphasizes this requirement in its response to comments to avoid inadvertently targeting non-signatory household members and to protect tenant rights in eviction-related filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — Moving-to-Work (MTW) agencies subject to rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All Moving-to-Work agencies and the housing they own, operate, manage, and administer are subject to this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD responds to commenters clarifying that MTW agencies are not excluded and must comply with the 30-day notice rule and related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHAs' responsibility for PBV recertifications and tenant assistance information
rubrics_metrics.description: PBV owners do not recertify tenant income and therefore may not possess information on applying for hardship exemptions or interim recertifications; PHAs, not owners, are responsible for ensuring PBV families understand when and how to request interim income recertifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD notes this operational distinction to clarify obligations and practical implementation; it supports coordination between owners and PHAs so tenants receive required information in notices and can access recertification/hardship processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers and PHA discretion regarding arrears forgiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs and owners may request waivers of regulations pursuant to 24 CFR 5.110; PHAs have the authority to forgive rent arrears, and the final rule does not limit PHAs' discretion in that regard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD acknowledges commenters' requests for waivers or carve-outs; explains procedures for waiver requests and confirms PHAs retain some programmatic flexibilities (e.g., forgiving arrears), but HUD declines program-wide automatic waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: HUD scope: RAD conversions and LIHTC — coverage limits and follow-up actions
rubrics_metrics.description: RAD-converted properties are governed by RAD Implementation Notices (PIH notices) which historically required at least 14 days' notice; HUD will amend the RAD Notice to reflect this rule's change for PBRA properties and address RAD PBV conversions. HUD states it does not have jurisdiction to establish rules governing properties supported under Treasury's Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion explains the rule's scope and HUD's approach to ensuring RAD-converted residents retain rights while acknowledging statutory or jurisdictional limits regarding LIHTC properties. HUD will take administrative steps (amend RAD Notice) to align program guidance where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement (not requirement) to provide information on local rental assistance resources
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD does not require PHAs or owners to provide tenants with a specific list of local nonprofit or rental assistance resources, but HUD encourages PHAs and owners to provide tenants facing eviction for nonpayment of rent with information regarding rental assistance resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD explains requiring a non-comprehensive list could cause unintended consequences; instead HUD encourages active cooperation with legal aid organizations and outreach by providers to inform tenants of available assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to cooperate with rental assistance applications and consider tolling the notice in pending applications/recertifications
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD expects PHAs and owners to be aware of pending recertifications or hardship exemptions and encourages cooperation with rent assistance programs (e.g., accepting rent assistance funds). Commenters urged tolling the 30-day period while applications are pending or prohibiting filing while assistance is processing; HUD emphasizes incorporation of attempts to obtain assistance into repayment plans and awareness of pending actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While HUD did not adopt a universal tolling requirement, it highlights expectations for cooperation and suggests PHAs/owners should incorporate assistance efforts into repayment agreements; HUD may consider issuing future guidance on best practices for nonpayment cases and potential abuse.
